issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Milkable interface (with messageOnMilk()), but the solution repository introduces an interface named Dairy (with messageOnMilk()) and the Milkable.java file in the solution is empty. The concrete animal classes (Goat, Seal) implement Dairy in the solution instead of Milkable. This name/type mismatch between Milkable and Dairy is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students and prevent them from matching the required design or using the provided template Main which expects Milkable.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across artifacts. Either (A) rename Dairy.java to Milkable.java and have Goat and Seal implement Milkable (ensuring messageOnMilk() signature matches the problem statement), and remove the empty Milkable.java; or (B) update the problem statement and template to use Dairy instead of Milkable. The simpler fix is to implement Milkable with messageOnMilk() in the solution and have the animal classes implement Milkable.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (with method messageOnMilk()), but the solution implementation provides an interface named 'Dairy' and has Goat and Seal implement 'Dairy'. This mismatches the expected identifier 'Milkable' and creates confusion for students who will look for/implement 'Milkable' based on the exercise description and template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the interface name across artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (and keep the method messageOnMilk()), update Goat and Seal to implement 'Milkable', and remove or repurpose any empty Milkable.java file in the solution repository so that the problem statement, template, and solution consistently use 'Milkable'.
